critical_issues.msg: poolclass=pool.NullPool disables connection pooling entirely — each migration acquires and discards a fresh connection, causing significant overhead on larger migrations.
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove poolclass=pool.NullPool and let SQLAlchemy use its default (QueuePool). If you need a non-default pool size, configure pool_size and max_overflow instead.

critical_issues.msg: Number(sessionId) returns NaN for non-numeric strings with no validation — crashes all downstream query keys and store lookups.
critical_issues.suggestion: Validate with isNaN or parse via Number.parseInt(sessionId, 10) and guard with a redirect if invalid.

critical_issues.msg: createSession.mutate(undefined, ...) sends undefined as the request body — if the backend requires a non-null body, this will 422 or 500, creating a new broken session every render.
critical_issues.suggestion: Pass an empty object {} as the body, or confirm the backend accepts null/undefined for session creation.

critical_issues.msg: PaginatedSessions defines total_pages but ChatMessage type at line 17 has no page metadata — these types are inconsistent with how messages are fetched (no pagination params sent, no pagination fields returned).
critical_issues.suggestion: Align PaginatedSessions with the actual endpoint behavior (getMessages returns {items, total} with no pagination fields), or remove total_pages if unused.

critical_issues.msg: ApiEnvelope<T> here wraps data as PaginatedResponse<T> (line 33-36), but useChatMessages (line 379) calls aiApi.getMessages which returns ApiEnvelope<{items, total}> — a type where data IS the raw {items,total} object, not a PaginatedResponse. The generic T cannot unify both shapes.
critical_issues.suggestion: Create a distinct response type for useChatMessages that maps correctly to the ai.ts return shape, or change the generic constraint so ai.ts ApiEnvelope and queries.ts ApiEnvelope are compatible.

critical_issues.msg: Markdown link component renders `target="_blank"` without `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, allowing the opened page to access `window.opener`.
critical_issues.suggestion: Add `rel="noopener noreferrer"` to the anchor element in the markdown `a` component override.

critical_issues.msg: tenant_id is null-checked with `ctx.tenant_id or 0`, silently coercing a missing tenant to 0 — a valid multi-tenant ID — which could cause data to be stored under the wrong tenant or bypass tenant isolation.
critical_issues.suggestion: Require a valid tenant_id; raise 401 Unauthorized if ctx.tenant_id is None instead of defaulting to 0.

critical_issues.msg: auth_headers_web calls await async_session.commit() directly, breaking the router-owned transaction boundary — service-layer code must not call commit (rule #121, #122).
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove the explicit commit call; the router-level get_db dependency handles commit/rollback automatically. If data must be visible within the same test, use flush() instead.

critical_issues.msg: auth_headers_tenant_2 calls await async_session.commit() directly, same violation as auth_headers_web (rule #121, #122).
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove the explicit commit; let the fixture-level session lifecycle handle it.

critical_issues.msg: Every test method calls await async_session.commit() explicitly — integration test services must not call commit (rule #121, #122); the get_db dependency already commits on normal exit.
critical_issues.suggestion: Remove all await async_session.commit() calls from test methods. Use await self.session.flush() only when auto-generated IDs are needed within the same test.

critical_issues.msg: TestAIEndpoints, TestCreateSession, and TestSendMessage never inject a mocked AIService — all HTTP tests (lines 70-88, 107-111) hit the auth guard and return 401/403 before reaching any router logic. The auth-only pass prevents testing actual endpoint behavior (rule #66, #67).
critical_issues.suggestion: Override require_auth in the FastAPI dependency_overrides dict: app.dependency_overrides[require_auth] = lambda: AuthContext(user_id=99, tenant_id=1, roles=[]). Then inject MockAIService via patching or a dependency override so endpoint handlers are actually exercised.

suggestions.msg: Step 1 references @types/react-syntax-highlighter but it is already in devDependencies (line 39 of frontend/package.json).
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the @types/react-syntax-highlighter addition from step 1 — it's already installed.

suggestions.msg: Plan references react-markdown version ^10.1.0 in package.json (already installed) but step 1 says to install react-markdown ^9 — version mismatch.
suggestions.suggestion: Update step 1 to reflect the already-installed versions: react-markdown ^10.1.0 and remark-gfm ^4.0.1 (no install needed).

suggestions.msg: Plan says to 'register in src/db/base.py' — but ai_session.py models already exist and are imported in db/models/__init__.py, not base.py. The plan's description of registration is inaccurate.
suggestions.suggestion: Clarify step 2: models are already created and exported from db/models/__init__.py. Only add to alembic/env.py if not already present.

suggestions.msg: package-lock.json is a generated file and not in .gitignore — it will be committed and diverge from package.json on every install, creating noise in diffs.
suggestions.suggestion: Add 'package-lock.json' to .gitignore, or add 'frontend/package-lock.json' to the repo-level .gitignore, since the project uses pnpm or npm's lockfile separately from the frontend directory.

suggestions.msg: This file is 370KB+ — it is too large to read directly and should not be manually edited. Consider using 'npm install --package-lock-only' to regenerate it rather than committing it.
suggestions.suggestion: If the project uses npm, add package-lock.json to .gitignore and only commit yarn.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml if those are the chosen package managers.

suggestions.msg: react-markdown is at ^10.1.0 but react-syntax-highlighter is at ^16.1.1 (a prerelease beta) — major version mismatch; react-syntax-highlighter v16 may have breaking API changes vs v15.
suggestions.suggestion: Pin react-syntax-highlighter to a stable compatible version (e.g. ^15.0.0) or verify v16 API is compatible with react-markdown ^10.1.0.

suggestions.msg: Types for react and react-dom are pinned to ^19 (caret), but @types/react-syntax-highlighter is pinned to ^15.5.13 (exact caret) — inconsistent major version alignment across type packages.
suggestions.suggestion: Align type package majors: if using React 19, use @types/react-syntax-highlighter ^16 or the equivalent major version for the installed package.

suggestions.msg: NaN sessionId (from line 14) makes messagesBySession[NaN] always undefined, silently falling through to the empty array — no error, just blank screen.
suggestions.suggestion: Guard at line 14 so NaN cannot propagate.

suggestions.msg: setMessages from useChatStore is a stable selector result, but the effect lacks a memoization guarantee — if the store shape changes between renders it could become stale.
suggestions.suggestion: Wrap the effect logic in useCallback or confirm setMessages is referentially stable from the store.

suggestions.msg: messages in the scroll-into-view effect dependency array is the store array; if a parent component causes re-renders without a message change, the effect fires unnecessarily.
suggestions.suggestion: Use a ref or a targeted dependency like messages.length to avoid unnecessary scroll triggers.

suggestions.msg: sendMessageMutation.onSuccess invalidates the messages query cache (line 405 in queries.ts), but the response from mutateAsync is also used to add the assistant message to the store directly — two sources of truth without coordination.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the store addMessage call and rely solely on the query cache invalidation + refetch, or remove the cache invalidation and keep only store-side state.

suggestions.msg: catch block swallows the error with no logging, making debugging impossible for production users.
suggestions.suggestion: Add console.error(err) or replace with a toast/notification to the user with the actual error detail.

suggestions.msg: onRegenerate={() => handleSend(m.content)} creates a new function reference per message render, defeating ChatMessage memoization.
suggestions.suggestion: Memoize the handler per message id, e.g. with useCallback(m.content, ...).

suggestions.msg: useEffect with no dependency array values (empty deps after eslint-disable) runs after every render, not just mount — in StrictMode it fires twice, creating two sessions.
suggestions.suggestion: Use a mount-only guard: useRef(false) to track if the effect has already run.

suggestions.msg: router.replace navigates to a URL that expects [sessionId] (plural: /ai/sessions/<id>) but the file is at /ai/[sessionId] (singular: /ai/<id>) — these routes are inconsistent.
suggestions.suggestion: Verify the correct target URL: /ai/sessions/${newId} vs /ai/${newId} must match the actual route file structure.

suggestions.msg: Mutation onSuccess callback does not handle errors from setActiveSession or router.replace — both can throw without being caught.
suggestions.suggestion: Wrap router.replace in a try/catch inside onSuccess.

suggestions.msg: ApiEnvelope<T> is identical to the one duplicated in queries.ts — any divergence causes a type mismatch in callers like useChatMessages which import aiApi but annotate with the queries.ts type.
suggestions.suggestion: Export a single shared ApiEnvelope type from one file and import it in both.

suggestions.msg: onSuccess invalidates the messages query cache but does not wait for the refetch — the session page already optimistically adds the assistant message to the store (page.tsx line 52), so after the cache invalidates and refetches, the store will receive a second duplicate of the same message from setMessages.
suggestions.suggestion: Either remove the store addMessage in page.tsx and rely purely on cache, or remove the cache invalidation and keep only store-side state — do not do both.

suggestions.msg: useReminders has a different ApiEnvelope shape (no <T> type param) compared to all other hooks — inconsistent typing across the module.
suggestions.suggestion: Apply the same ApiEnvelope<T> pattern used by all other hooks to useReminders for consistency.

suggestions.msg: DOM manipulation (`document.getElementById` + classList.toggle) bypasses React state, risking desync if panel visibility is later controlled by state.
suggestions.suggestion: Move panel visibility into `useChatStore` (e.g. `isPanelOpen`) and drive the class from that state instead of direct DOM manipulation.

suggestions.msg: DOM manipulation for close button mirrors the FAB issue — same React-state-desync risk.
suggestions.suggestion: Use shared React state (e.g. `isPanelOpen` in the store) so both FAB and close button update the same source of truth.

suggestions.msg: Comment describes what code already does rather than why it was written that way.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the comment — the store usage is self-evident from the code.

suggestions.msg: handleSuggestion sets the input text but immediately after the user must manually press Enter or click Send; the UX flow is not seamless.
suggestions.suggestion: Consider auto-triggering send after setting the suggestion text, or document that the user must press Enter to submit.

suggestions.msg: Copy button handler closes over `code` from the JSX render, not from the event — if the message re-renders between click and execution the copy could capture a stale value.
suggestions.suggestion: Read `message.content` inside the click handler directly instead of the closed-over `code` variable, or use a ref.

suggestions.msg: handleNewConversation silently swallows errors — if session creation fails the user gets no feedback.
suggestions.suggestion: Add error feedback, e.g. `toast.error('Failed to create conversation')` from a toast library, or surface an inline error state.

suggestions.msg: handleDelete silently swallows errors — if deletion fails the local `deletingId` is still cleared, leaving a stale session in the list with no error signal.
suggestions.suggestion: Move `setDeletingId(null)` into the `try` block and add error feedback in the `catch` block.

suggestions.msg: useCreateChatSession is imported on line 6 and again on line 7 from the same module — duplicate import.
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the second import and keep only the consolidated import on line 6.

suggestions.msg: Clean, minimal typing indicator component with no issues.
clearAll() omits isLoading, leaving it at whatever value it had before the reset.
suggestions.suggestion: Include isLoading: false in the clearAll() set call, or explicitly reset all fields to their initial values.

suggestions.msg: clearSession(sessionId) clears messages but leaves activeSessionId unchanged — if the cleared session was active, the store holds a stale active pointer with no messages.
suggestions.suggestion: Consider also clearing activeSessionId when clearing the currently active session, or document the intended behavior explicitly.

suggestions.msg: Clean aggregator module with clear router exports and no issues.
Helper functions _session_to_dict and _message_to_dict reimplement .to_dict() which the docstring says models already have; this duplicates serialization logic in the router layer.
suggestions.suggestion: Replace _session_to_dict and _message_to_dict with direct calls to session.to_dict() and msg.to_dict() on the ORM objects returned by AIService.

suggestions.msg: SendMessageRequest.regenerate is accepted but never used in send_message.
suggestions.suggestion: Either implement the regenerate behavior or remove the field from the request model.

suggestions.msg: Magic number 10000 in max_length should be a named constant to make the limit easy to find and adjust.
suggestions.suggestion: Define MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 10000 as a module-level constant and reference it in the Field.

suggestions.msg: Magic number 0 used as sentinel in total_pages guard; the expression (total + page_size - 1) // page_size also handles page_size=0 implicitly.
suggestions.suggestion: Raise ValidationException for page_size <= 0 upstream rather than guarding with a conditional.

suggestions.msg: AIService is imported and used throughout but never explicitly called in a type annotation — the file does not validate that it actually provides create_session, list_sessions, delete_session, get_messages, and save_message.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a unit or integration test that exercises these endpoints with a mock or real AIService to catch missing methods at test time.

suggestions.msg: Clean re-export file that properly exposes all ORM models including ChatSessionModel and ChatMessageModel.
ChatMessageModel.role is a free-form String(20) with no enum or CHECK constraint, allowing any string value despite the comment documenting only 'user' or 'assistant'.
suggestions.suggestion: Use an Enum column type: role: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20), nullable=False) → from sqlalchemy import Enum; role: Mapped[Literal['user','assistant']] = mapped_column(Enum('user','assistant'), nullable=False)

suggestions.msg: generic_exception_handler logs exc type and str but omits request metadata (e.g. method, client IP) making post-mortem debugging harder for unhandled exceptions.
suggestions.suggestion: Add request scope details to the log call: logger.error("unhandled_exception", type=type(exc).__name__, detail=str(exc), path=request.url.path, method=request.method)

suggestions.msg: http_exception_handler does not log HTTP exceptions, so 4xx errors are invisible in structured logs and harder to investigate.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a logger call before returning: logger.warning("http_exception", status=exc.status_code, detail=exc.detail, path=request.url.path)

suggestions.msg: save_message accepts role as an unvalidated str parameter; a caller could pass any value (e.g. 'admin'), producing a ChatMessageModel with a role that never appears in message history consumption logic.
suggestions.suggestion: Add runtime validation: if role not in ('user', 'assistant'): raise ValidationException('role must be user or assistant')

suggestions.msg: generate_title returns a title longer than 50 characters when a single token (e.g. a long word or URL) exceeds that limit before splitting, since the truncation occurs after whitespace-normalized joining.
suggestions.suggestion: Move truncation before joining or apply it after: title = (' '.join(text.split()))[:50]

suggestions.msg: db_session.updated_at = now is assigned without an explicit flush call at that point; the subsequent flush on line 106 will persist it, but being implicit reduces clarity.
suggestions.suggestion: Add an inline comment noting the pending change will be flushed with the message, or add await self.session.flush() immediately after line 104.

suggestions.msg: save_message takes tenant_id but not user_id, so there is no user-level audit trail on individual messages; authorship must be derived via the session relationship.
suggestions.suggestion: If message-level user attribution is needed for compliance, add a user_id column to ChatMessageModel and accept it as a parameter here.

suggestions.msg: Global mutable module-level state (_tenant_id_web, _tenant_id_2_web) persists across the entire test session — cross-test contamination is possible if any test exits without resetting (rule #28).
suggestions.suggestion: Replace module-level globals with a shared-in-memory store (e.g., a class or dict on the conftest module) that clears on session end, or use pytest's `cached_setup` / a class-scoped fixture.

suggestions.msg: api_client fixture mutates the shared function-scoped `client` fixture in place (client.headers.update), which can leak headers into other tests that also use `client` (rule #28).
suggestions.suggestion: Clone headers instead of mutating the shared fixture: build a fresh AsyncClient per fixture, or copy headers into a new dict and return that without modifying the original client object.

suggestions.msg: AsyncGenerator is imported twice — once at line 27 (from collections.abc) and again at line 298. Minor redundancy (rule #20).
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the second import at line 298; the first import covers it.

suggestions.msg: Hardcoded user_id=999 bypasses the UserModel constraint (user_id references users.id). If the users table has a FK or the model requires a valid user, this creates an integrity risk — the test passes in CI but may fail against a strictly-validated schema (rule #50).
suggestions.suggestion: Create a real user via UserService and use its actual ID, matching the pattern used in auth_headers_web (lines 342-369 in conftest).

suggestions.msg: test_send_message_and_get asserts the canned placeholder response text 'AI integration is coming soon' — this tests a known-short-term stub, not actual AI behavior, making the test a false positive that will silently break once real AI is wired (rule #69, #70).
suggestions.suggestion: Either mock AIService.send_message to return a controlled response, or accept that this test must be updated when real AI is integrated. At minimum, document the placeholder nature.

suggestions.msg: Tests named *_requires_auth only verify that bare unauthenticated requests are rejected — they test the auth middleware, not the router. This is valuable but the test names are misleading (rule #67).
suggestions.suggestion: Rename to test_<endpoint>_unauthenticated_rejected to clarify what is being tested.

suggestions.msg: test_create_session_returns_envelope accepts 200, 401, or 403 as valid — this makes it a no-op that passes regardless of actual behavior (rule #65).
suggestions.suggestion: Override require_auth so the test exercises the actual create_session handler and asserts the specific 201 response shape.

suggestions.msg: MockAIService class is defined but never wired into the app via dependency override or monkeypatch — it is dead code in this test file (rule #17).
suggestions.suggestion: Either wire MockAIService into the app's dependency_overrides (replacing AIService) or remove the class definition.

suggestions.msg: The auth_headers fixture is defined but never used by any test in this file (rule #17).
suggestions.suggestion: Remove the unused fixture.

suggestions.msg: test_save_message_adds_and_flushes sets mock_session.execute to return mock_session_obj but then checks result.role == 'user' — the result is the ChatMessageModel returned by save_message, so the mock_session_obj title assertion is never checked, making the test pass without validating the title-set-on-session logic (rule #65, #69).
suggestions.suggestion: Assert that mock_session_obj.title was set after save_message completes: assert mock_session_obj.title is not None (or a specific expected title string).

suggestions.msg: test_update_session_title_returns_correct_value only verifies the mock's title attribute (set by the test itself) rather than exercising the actual service code path where session.title = title is assigned. The mock returns itself as the session so assertions are tautological (rule #65, #69).
suggestions.suggestion: Use a verifying mock (unittest.mock.PropertyMock or a side_effect on scalar_one_or_none) to capture the session object passed to get_session, then assert on that captured object's title attribute after the call.

suggestions.msg: TestCreateSession defines its own mock_session fixture which is identical to the one in TestSaveAndGetMessages and TestDeleteSession and TestUpdateSessionTitle — four copies of the same fixture could be consolidated into a shared class fixture or module-scoped fixture (rule #110).
suggestions.suggestion: Move the mock_session fixture to the class level using @pytest.fixture(scope='class') or define it once at module level.

warnings.msg: Comment describes what code already does rather than why it was written that way.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the comment — the store usage is self-evident from the code.

warnings.msg: handleSuggestion sets the input text but immediately after the user must manually press Enter or click Send; the UX flow is not seamless.
warnings.suggestion: Consider auto-triggering send after setting the suggestion text, or document that the user must press Enter to submit.

warnings.msg: Copy button handler closes over `code` from the JSX render, not from the event — if the message re-renders between click and execution the copy could capture a stale value.
warnings.suggestion: Read `message.content` inside the click handler directly instead of the closed-over `code` variable, or use a ref.

warnings.msg: handleNewConversation silently swallows errors — if session creation fails the user gets no feedback.
warnings.suggestion: Add error feedback, e.g. `toast.error('Failed to create conversation')` from a toast library, or surface an inline error state.

warnings.msg: handleDelete silently swallows errors — if deletion fails the local `deletingId` is still cleared, leaving a stale session in the list with no error signal.
warnings.suggestion: Move `setDeletingId(null)` into the `try` block and add error feedback in the `catch` block.

warnings.msg: useCreateChatSession is imported on line 6 and again on line 7 from the same module — duplicate import.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the second import and keep only the consolidated import on line 6.

warnings.msg: Clean, minimal typing indicator component with no issues.
clearAll() omits isLoading, leaving it at whatever value it had before the reset.
warnings.suggestion: Include isLoading: false in the clearAll() set call, or explicitly reset all fields to their initial values.

warnings.msg: clearSession(sessionId) clears messages but leaves activeSessionId unchanged — if the cleared session was active, the store holds a stale active pointer with no messages.
warnings.suggestion: Consider also clearing activeSessionId when clearing the currently active session, or document the intended behavior explicitly.

warnings.msg: Clean aggregator module with clear router exports and no issues.
Helper functions _session_to_dict and _message_to_dict reimplement .to_dict() which the docstring says models already have; this duplicates serialization logic in the router layer.
warnings.suggestion: Replace _session_to_dict and _message_to_dict with direct calls to session.to_dict() and msg.to_dict() on the ORM objects returned by AIService.

warnings.msg: SendMessageRequest.regenerate is accepted but never used in send_message.
warnings.suggestion: Either implement the regenerate behavior or remove the field from the request model.

warnings.msg: Magic number 10000 in max_length should be a named constant to make the limit easy to find and adjust.
warnings.suggestion: Define MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 10000 as a module-level constant and reference it in the Field.

warnings.msg: Magic number 0 used as sentinel in total_pages guard; the expression (total + page_size - 1) // page_size also handles page_size=0 implicitly.
warnings.suggestion: Raise ValidationException for page_size <= 0 upstream rather than guarding with a conditional.

warnings.msg: AIService is imported and used throughout but never explicitly called in a type annotation — the file does not validate that it actually provides create_session, list_sessions, delete_session, get_messages, and save_message.
warnings.suggestion: Add a unit or integration test that exercises these endpoints with a mock or real AIService to catch missing methods at test time.

warnings.msg: Clean re-export file that properly exposes all ORM models including ChatSessionModel and ChatMessageModel.

warnings.suggestion: Use an Enum column type: role: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(20), nullable=False) → from sqlalchemy import Enum; role: Mapped[Literal['user','assistant']] = mapped_column(Enum('user','assistant'), nullable=False)

warnings.msg: generic_exception_handler logs exc type and str but omits request metadata (e.g. method, client IP) making post-mortem debugging harder for unhandled exceptions.
warnings.suggestion: Add request scope details to the log call: logger.error("unhandled_exception", type=type(exc).__name__, detail=str(exc), path=request.url.path, method=request.method)

warnings.suggestion: Add a logger call before returning: logger.warning("http_exception", status=exc.status_code, detail=exc.detail, path=request.url.path)

warnings.msg: save_message accepts role as an unvalidated str parameter; a caller could pass any value (e.g. 'admin'), producing a ChatMessageModel with a role that never appears in message history consumption logic.
warnings.suggestion: Add runtime validation: if role not in ('user', 'assistant'): raise ValidationException('role must be user or assistant')

warnings.msg: generate_title returns a title longer than 50 characters when a single token (e.g. a long word or URL) exceeds that limit before splitting, since the truncation occurs after whitespace-normalized joining.
warnings.suggestion: Move truncation before joining or apply it after: title = (' '.join(text.split()))[:50]

warnings.msg: db_session.updated_at = now is assigned without an explicit flush call at that point; the subsequent flush on line 106 will persist it, but being implicit reduces clarity.
warnings.suggestion: Add an inline comment noting the pending change will be flushed with the message, or add await self.session.flush() immediately after line 104.

warnings.msg: save_message takes tenant_id but not user_id, so there is no user-level audit trail on individual messages; authorship must be derived via the session relationship.
warnings.suggestion: If message-level user attribution is needed for compliance, add a user_id column to ChatMessageModel and accept it as a parameter here.

warnings.msg: Global mutable module-level state (_tenant_id_web, _tenant_id_2_web) persists across the entire test session — cross-test contamination is possible if any test exits without resetting (rule #28).
warnings.suggestion: Replace module-level globals with a shared-in-memory store (e.g., a class or dict on the conftest module) that clears on session end, or use pytest's `cached_setup` / a class-scoped fixture.

warnings.msg: api_client fixture mutates the shared function-scoped `client` fixture in place (client.headers.update), which can leak headers into other tests that also use `client` (rule #28).
warnings.suggestion: Clone headers instead of mutating the shared fixture: build a fresh AsyncClient per fixture, or copy headers into a new dict and return that without modifying the original client object.

warnings.msg: AsyncGenerator is imported twice — once at line 27 (from collections.abc) and again at line 298. Minor redundancy (rule #20).
warnings.suggestion: Remove the second import at line 298; the first import covers it.

warnings.msg: Hardcoded user_id=999 bypasses the UserModel constraint (user_id references users.id). If the users table has a FK or the model requires a valid user, this creates an integrity risk — the test passes in CI but may fail against a strictly-validated schema (rule #50).
warnings.suggestion: Create a real user via UserService and use its actual ID, matching the pattern used in auth_headers_web (lines 342-369 in conftest).

warnings.msg: test_send_message_and_get asserts the canned placeholder response text 'AI integration is coming soon' — this tests a known-short-term stub, not actual AI behavior, making the test a false positive that will silently break once real AI is wired (rule #69, #70).
warnings.suggestion: Either mock AIService.send_message to return a controlled response, or accept that this test must be updated when real AI is integrated. At minimum, document the placeholder nature.

warnings.msg: Tests named *_requires_auth only verify that bare unauthenticated requests are rejected — they test the auth middleware, not the router. This is valuable but the test names are misleading (rule #67).

warnings.msg: test_create_session_returns_envelope accepts 200, 401, or 403 as valid — this makes it a no-op that passes regardless of actual behavior (rule #65).

warnings.msg: MockAIService class is defined but never wired into the app via dependency override or monkeypatch — it is dead code in this test file (rule #17).
warnings.suggestion: Either wire MockAIService into the app's dependency_overrides (replacing AIService) or remove the class definition.

warnings.msg: The auth_headers fixture is defined but never used by any test in this file (rule #17).
warnings.suggestion: Remove the unused fixture.

warnings.msg: test_save_message_adds_and_flushes sets mock_session.execute to return mock_session_obj but then checks result.role == 'user' — the result is the ChatMessageModel returned by save_message, so the mock_session_obj title assertion is never checked, making the test pass without validating the title-set-on-session logic (rule #65, #69).
warnings.suggestion: Assert that mock_session_obj.title was set after save_message completes: assert mock_session_obj.title is not None (or a specific expected title string).

warnings.msg: test_update_session_title_returns_correct_value only verifies the mock's title attribute (set by the test itself) rather than exercising the actual service code path where session.title = title is assigned. warnings.suggestion: Use a verifying mock (unittest.mock.PropertyMock or a side_effect on scalar_one_or_none) to capture the session object passed to get_session, then assert on that captured object's title attribute after the call.

issues.message: Number(sessionId) returns NaN for non-numeric strings with no validation — crashes all downstream query keys and store lookups.
issues.suggestion: Validate with isNaN or parse via Number.parseInt(sessionId, 10) and guard with a redirect if invalid.

issues.message: NaN sessionId (from line 14) makes messagesBySession[NaN] always undefined, silently falling through to the empty array — no error, just blank screen.
issues.suggestion: Guard at line 14 so NaN cannot propagate.

issues.message: setMessages from useChatStore is a stable selector result, but the effect lacks a memoization guarantee — if the store shape changes between renders it could become stale.
issues.suggestion: Wrap the effect logic in useCallback or confirm setMessages is referentially stable from the store.

issues.message: messages in the scroll-into-view effect dependency array is the store array; if a parent component causes re-renders without a message change, the effect fires unnecessarily.
issues.suggestion: Use a ref or a targeted dependency like messages.length to avoid unnecessary scroll triggers.

issues.message: sendMessageMutation.onSuccess invalidates the messages query cache (line 405 in queries.ts), but the response from mutateAsync is also used to add the assistant message to the store directly — two sources of truth without coordination.
issues.suggestion: Remove the store addMessage call and rely solely on the query cache invalidation + refetch, or remove the cache invalidation and keep only store-side state.

issues.message: catch block swallows the error with no logging, making debugging impossible for production users.
issues.suggestion: Add console.error(err) or replace with a toast/notification to the user with the actual error detail.

issues.message: onRegenerate={() => handleSend(m.content)} creates a new function reference per message render, defeating ChatMessage memoization.
issues.suggestion: Memoize the handler per message id, e.g. with useCallback(m.content, ...).

parsed.summary: NaN from Number(sessionId) is the critical failure path; no validation exists and it silently produces a blank screen. Secondary issues are store/Query cache dual writes and missing error diagnostics.

issues.message: createSession.mutate(undefined, ...) sends undefined as the request body — if the backend requires a non-null body, this will 422 or 500, creating a new broken session every render.
issues.suggestion: Pass an empty object {} as the body, or confirm the backend accepts null/undefined for session creation.

issues.message: useEffect with no dependency array values (empty deps after eslint-disable) runs after every render, not just mount — in StrictMode it fires twice, creating two sessions.
issues.suggestion: Use a mount-only guard: useRef(false) to track if the effect has already run.

issues.message: router.replace navigates to a URL that expects [sessionId] (plural: /ai/sessions/<id>) but the file is at /ai/[sessionId] (singular: /ai/<id>) — these routes are inconsistent.
issues.suggestion: Verify the correct target URL: /ai/sessions/${newId} vs /ai/${newId} must match the actual route file structure.

issues.message: Mutation onSuccess callback does not handle errors from setActiveSession or router.replace — both can throw without being caught.
issues.suggestion: Wrap router.replace in a try/catch inside onSuccess.

parsed.summary: mutate(undefined) is likely wrong and will cause a backend 422. The empty useEffect deps fire on every render (StrictMode = double session creation), and the routing target URL may not match the route file.

parsed.summary: Type definitions don't match actual endpoint behavior (messages are paginated in shape but not in API usage), and the duplicate ApiEnvelope risks type mismatches at call sites.

parsed.summary: Good coverage of session lifecycle, tenant isolation, and error cases, but every test has spurious explicit commit() calls and uses hardcoded user IDs instead of real seeded users.

issues.message: TestAIEndpoints, TestCreateSession, and TestSendMessage never inject a mocked AIService — all HTTP tests (lines 70-88, 107-111) hit the auth guard and return 401/403 before reaching any router logic. The auth-only pass prevents testing actual endpoint behavior (rule #66, #67).
issues.suggestion: Override require_auth in the FastAPI dependency_overrides dict: app.dependency_overrides[require_auth] = lambda: AuthContext(user_id=99, tenant_id=1, roles=[]). Then inject MockAIService via patching or a dependency override so endpoint handlers are actually exercised.

issues.message: Tests named *_requires_auth only verify that bare unauthenticated requests are rejected — they test the auth middleware, not the router. This is valuable but the test names are misleading (rule #67).
issues.suggestion: Rename to test_<endpoint>_unauthenticated_rejected to clarify what is being tested.

issues.message: test_create_session_returns_envelope accepts 200, 401, or 403 as valid — this makes it a no-op that passes regardless of actual behavior (rule #65).
issues.suggestion: Override require_auth so the test exercises the actual create_session handler and asserts the specific 201 response shape.

issues.message: MockAIService class is defined but never wired into the app via dependency override or monkeypatch — it is dead code in this test file (rule #17).
issues.suggestion: Either wire MockAIService into the app's dependency_overrides (replacing AIService) or remove the class definition.

issues.message: The auth_headers fixture is defined but never used by any test in this file (rule #17).
issues.suggestion: Remove the unused fixture.

parsed.summary: Helper functions and Pydantic validation tests are well-structured, but all HTTP endpoint tests fail at auth before reaching router/service logic due to missing dependency overrides.

issues.message: test_save_message_adds_and_flushes sets mock_session.execute to return mock_session_obj but then checks result.role == 'user' — the result is the ChatMessageModel returned by save_message, so the mock_session_obj title assertion is never checked, making the test pass without validating the title-set-on-session logic (rule #65, #69).
issues.suggestion: Assert that mock_session_obj.title was set after save_message completes: assert mock_session_obj.title is not None (or a specific expected title string).

issues.message: test_update_session_title_returns_correct_value only verifies the mock's title attribute (set by the test itself) rather than exercising the actual service code path where session.title = title is assigned. The mock returns itself as the session so assertions are tautological (rule #65, #69).
issues.suggestion: Use a verifying mock (unittest.mock.PropertyMock or a side_effect on scalar_one_or_none) to capture the session object passed to get_session, then assert on that captured object's title attribute after the call.

issues.message: TestCreateSession defines its own mock_session fixture which is identical to the one in TestSaveAndGetMessages and TestDeleteSession and TestUpdateSessionTitle — four copies of the same fixture could be consolidated into a shared class fixture or module-scoped fixture (rule #110).
issues.suggestion: Move the mock_session fixture to the class level using @pytest.fixture(scope='class') or define it once at module level.

parsed.summary: generate_title tests are thorough and well-structured; flush/add assertions are correct, but mock return-value assertions are too loose and don't verify the service actually modified the session state.
